input.question: What is the evolutionary purpose of having different blood types (A,B,AB,O)?
input.ground_truth: While this doesn't answer your question, it is important to understand that evolution does not have a purpose. Mutations do not happen because they can be beneficial. Random mutations happen in individuals, then over time if the mutation is beneficial and propagated via offspring, the lineage with that trait may be more fit than individuals without that trait and slowly become more predominant. A more accurate question would be "Why did organisms evolve different blood types?" I'm not trying to be pedantic for the sake of pedantry, but I think maybe this will help you understand other's answers a little more clearly.

Okay! Imagine your blood is like a team of little helpers that travel around your body to keep you healthy. Each person’s blood has a special “tag” on these helpers, and there are different kinds of tags—like stickers! We call these “blood types”: A, B, AB, and O.

Long, long ago, people had different kinds of these tags because it helped them survive in different ways. For example, if some people got sick from a certain kind of germ, having a different tag on their blood helped their bodies fight off that germ better. So, over a long, long time, people with different tags (blood types) survived and had babies, and that’s how we got many different blood types today.

It’s a bit like how some people have brown eyes and some have blue eyes—different kinds help us all be a little different and stronger as a big group!
